name: Eligibility gate mixin
description: Methods on the autopilot pass that decide, in order, daily budget, whether the quest is due (asked of the hub's Proactivity: its cadence in its zone, a Run now, a reactive trigger from the asks Quest events report), roster day and backpressure, and read open asks, so a quest is skipped with a reason before any goal is read.
advantages: Cheap, ordered and explainable gates that follow the person's settings exactly.
disadvantages: The ordering and interplay of many rules is intricate, and a new setting needs a matching case.

name: Single-purpose routines
description: A quest's named single-purpose autopilots beside its ordinary one: each routine has a purpose (the one kind of work), its own instructions, days and hour (the hub's Proactivity, as a window) and the purpose's own gate, which refuses a pass with nothing due. A pass writes only its one work task and its own bookkeeping, never a goal, a task or a plan. The learning purpose asks the hub's Learning what reviews are due.
advantages: A quest can keep a daily worker and a weekly reviewer without either inheriting the other's work; a quiet week costs one stamp and no model call; a new purpose is one registered object.
disadvantages: A routine is a second schedule to keep in mind beside the quest's own, and the work text is a prompt, so staying inside the purpose is instructed, not enforced by tool permissions.
